title: Hormuz Day 69 · TTF €44.21 · MOU Talks Alive But Trump 'Not Satisfied'
hook: The Strait of Hormuz has been closed for 69+ days. US-Iran exchanged fire on May 7 yet Trump declared hostilities 'terminated.' A 14-point MOU is in play. The market is gridlocked — but not for long.
details:
European gas opened the week at a crossroads. TTF front-month closed at €44.21/MWh (close 08 May, Thu), barely moved on the week, per Trading Economics / ICE. Henry Hub at $2.82/MMBtu, JKM at $16.84/MMBtu. Brent crude holds above $100/bbl.

The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed for the 69th consecutive day after a failed brief reopening on April 21-22 collapsed within 24 hours. Neither the US nor Iran has removed their respective blockades. Axios reports a 14-point MOU is being negotiated via Pakistani intermediaries, but The Guardian notes Trump said he's 'not satisfied' with the terms.

Below you'll find 8 analysis cards covering price action, weather & demand, storage, LNG flows, power & carbon, geopolitics, scenario analysis, and risk outlook — plus trade ideas on every card.

title: Welcome Back
details: After a month-long pause, the Gas Morning Brief returns to your screens. The gas market has evolved since our April 12 edition: the ceasefire has held (barely), Hormuz remains shut, TTF has drifted from €43 to €44, and the world has learned to live with a $100 oil price. But below the surface calm, the fundamentals are worsening. Storage is at 34%. Qatar is still offline. The MOU talks are fragile. This is not a market at peace — it's a market holding its breath. Today's edition: 8 cards, 24 trade ideas, and one message: the break is coming, and you need to be positioned before it does. — La Rédaction 🦊

title: TTF Holds €44 as Ceasefire Dance Enters Decisive Phase — But War Premium Refuses to Die
hook: TTF closed at €44.21/MWh (close 08 Fri) — barely moved on the week despite exchange of fire between US and Iran. Henry Hub at $2.82 — still a different planet. JKM drops to $16.84.
author: Blaise 🧮
details:
TTF front-month closed at €44.21/MWh (close 08 May, Thu), ▲+0.55 vs prev week, per Trading Economics / ICE Endex. Over the past month, TTF is down 5.46% but remains +26.14% YoY. NBP settled at 107.87 GBp/thm (close 08 May), ▲+0.94% on the day, down 7.61% on the month, per ICE NBP data. The market is in a holding pattern: neither the ceasefire optimists nor the escalation bears can establish control.

Hormuz Day 69+ and still effectively closed. As of early May 2026, the Strait has been shut to commercial shipping for 69+ days after a failed brief reopening on April 21-22 that collapsed within 24 hours, per Discovery Alert. The House of Commons Library confirms that while a conditional ceasefire is in place, "almost no shipping has used the strait and it remains effectively closed". About 20,000 mariners and 2,000 ships remain stranded in the Persian Gulf per IMO reporting.

Across the Atlantic: Henry Hub at $2.82/MMBtu. US natgas futures fell to $2.82, near a four-week high but still depressed, supported by declining output as major producers (EQT) scale back activity, per Trading Economics. Henry Hub spot last reported at $2.67/MMBtu (settle 04 May), per FRED / EIA. US gas rigs at 129, ▲+21 YoY, while the total rig count rose by one to 548 in the week to May 8, per Baker Hughes / BOE Report. The US gas complex remains functionally disconnected from European geopolitical risk.

Asia: JKM falls to $16.84/MMBtu (close 07 May). Down 13.60% on the month but still +47.07% YoY, per Trading Economics. The decline reflects a mix of demand destruction in Asia, new US LNG supply (Golden Pass first cargo), and some expectation of eventual Hormuz resolution. But the JKM-TTF spread remains wide at ~$12-13/MMBtu equivalent.

Brent crude at $100.49/bbl (close 08 May), ▲+4.76% MoM, ▲+57.24% YoY, per Trading Economics. Oil's resilience above $100 — despite ceasefire hopes — signals the market isn't buying the peace narrative either.

💡 Trade Ideas

1. Long TTF Volatility — Buy June €40 Put + €50 Call Straddle: Binary outcome risk is maximal. Straddle costs ~€2.50-3.00. Break-even at €37.50 or €53. Payoff is asymmetric.

2. Short Jun TTF €38 Puts / Long Jun TTF €50 Calls (Risk Reversal): Express bullish skew cheaply. Collect €0.60-0.80 on put sale, fund €50 call. Net cost ~€0.20-0.40. Unlimited upside above €50.

3. Long JKM-TTF Spread for Q3 2026: If Hormuz partially reopens, Qatar prioritizes Asian lifters, widening spread from ~$12 to $15+/MMBtu.

title: Mild-May Bias Across Europe, But El Niño Watch Steals the Long-Range Spotlight
hook: Mean temperatures running 0.5-2°C above normal for May. Nordic hydro deficit persists but spring melt is improving. El Niño 61% probability by July — potentially a Super El Niño by winter.
author: Sage 🦎
details:
May weather across Europe: above-normal temperatures dominate. Mean temperatures are running 0.5–2°C above climate normals, per Pogodnik. Day-ahead power prices hit multi-month lows: British, Nordic, Dutch at €6.85, €7.61, €14.46/MWh respectively — lowest since Oct 2025, per Euronews.

Nordic hydro deficit persists. Norway's winter snow drought — worst since 1996 — created ~25 TWh deficit. Spring melt underway but inflows thin. Nordic power prices surged 4x earlier in 2026 but have moderated.

El Niño Watch: 61% probability by May-July, Super El Niño increasingly likely. NOAA CPC active El Niño Watch. ECMWF ensemble trending stronger. Weather.com reports Super El Niño (Niño 3.4 > +2.0°C) increasingly plausible. Next NOAA update: May 14.

💡 Trade Ideas

1. Sell TTF Dec '26 / Jan '27 Calendar Spread (Mild Winter Play): El Niño historically means milder NW European winters. Current flat curve makes this cheap.

2. Long EU Carbon / Short TTF (Clean Dark Spread Play): EUA at €75.18 ▲+1.98% MoM. Carbon strength + weak power demand = coal displacement, reducing gas-for-power.

3. Long Nordic Power vs Short TTF (Relative Value): Hydro deficit constrains power exports, widening Nordpool-TTF spread.

title: EU Storage at ~34% — Injection Season Underway but Pace Is Everything
hook: EU gas storage at 34.3%, well below 5-year average. To hit 90% November mandate, Europe needs ~3,462 GWh/day. With Hormuz closed and TTF at €44, the economics are painful.
author: La Rédaction 🦊
details:
EU aggregate gas storage at approximately 34.3% full — significantly below 5-year average, per EnergyRiskIQ / AGSI+. Required injection: ~3,462 GWh/day for 90% by Nov 1. Maximum capacity: ~4,200 GWh/day — virtually no margin.

Constraining factors: TTF at ~€44 makes injection expensive; Hormuz closure strands ~20% of global LNG; EU Russian LNG spot ban (in effect since April 25) removes ~9 bcm/yr; Qatar's Ras Laffan under force majeure with full restoration unlikely before end-August.

💡 Trade Ideas

1. Long TTF Calendar — Buy Dec 2026 / Sell Jun 2026: Winter must price in refill risk. Buy Dec at €44.10, sell Jun at €44.21. Target spread widening to €5-10.

2. Long TTF Summer '26 Volatility: Any injection disruption spikes near-dated TTF. Summer implied vol likely underpriced.

3. Storage Arbitrage — Fixed-Price Injection Strip: Lock in TTF summer prices (~€43-44) for injection now. If TTF spikes in Q3, spread between fixed cost and winter spot widens.

title: Golden Pass Ships First Cargo as US LNG Hits Overdrive — But Can It Replace Qatar?
hook: Golden Pass LNG (9th US export terminal) ships first cargo. EIA expects record US LNG exports in 2026. But 20% of global LNG remains stranded by Hormuz — US growth can't bridge the gap.
author: Sage 🦎
details:
Golden Pass LNG ships first cargo. The 9th US export terminal enters service with third-highest nominal capacity behind Sabine Pass (3.6 Bcf/d) and Plaquemines (2.6 Bcf/d), per gCaptain / EIA. Train 2 startup targeted for later 2026.

EIA expects record US LNG exports in 2026 with higher utilization, driven by Hormuz-related demand from Europe and Asia, per EIA Today in Energy.

But Qatar gap persists: QatarEnergy says damage could take 5 years. Wood Mackenzie: full Ras Laffan restoration by end-August at earliest. Two trains permanently damaged. Hormuz adds $2-3/MMBtu to freight costs.

JKM at $16.84/MMBtu (close 07 May), ▼-13.60% MoM but ▲+47.07% YoY.

💡 Trade Ideas

1. Long LNG Freight Rates (FFA Q3 2026): Cape routing premium persists if Hormuz closed. Target $2-3/MMBtu premium.

2. Long TTF / Short JKM (Europe Premium): EU Russian ban + Hormuz = tighter European physical market. Golden Pass cargoes to Europe compress TTF-JKM spread.

3. Long US LNG Exporter Equities: Higher utilization + elevated prices = margin expansion for Venture Global, Cheniere.

title: Negative Power Prices Sweep Europe — But the Gas-Carbon Dynamic Is Shifting
hook: Day-ahead power hit €6.85/MWh in the UK, €7.61/MWh in Nordics. EU carbon at €75.18. Solar spring surge crushing spark spreads, but coal-to-gas switching still supports gas at the margin.
author: Henry 🦉
details:
Day-ahead power at multi-month lows: UK €6.85, Nordics €7.61, Dutch €14.46/MWh — lowest since Oct 2025, per Euronews. Negative prices occurring across several zones.

EU carbon (EUA) at €75.18 (close 08 May), ▲+0.07% DoD, ▲+1.98% MoM, ▲+6.80% YoY, per Trading Economics. MSR continues withdrawing allowances. EUA Dec '26 at ~€73.04 (backwardation).

Clean dark spread near zero: At EUA €75, coal uneconomic for baseload in Germany/Netherlands. Gas remains marginal fuel but squeezed by solar during daytime hours. Evening ramp (17-20h CET) creates gas demand premium.

💡 Trade Ideas

1. Long EUA Dec '26 — Carbon Upside: MSR tightening + reduced free allocations. Target €80+ by Q4.

2. Intraday Power Spread — Buy Evening Peak / Sell Solar Noon (Germany): Solar-duck-curve creates €15-25/MWh spread in summer.

3. Short German Power / Long TTF (Spark Spread Compression): If TTF rises while solar suppresses power, spark spread compresses further.

title: One-Page MOU, Terminated Hostilities, and a Strait Still Closed — The Fog of Negotiation
hook: US and Iran exchange fire on May 7 but Trump declares hostilities 'terminated.' A 14-point MOU via Pakistan intermediaries. Hormuz remains closed. Neither side removed blockades.
author: Henry 🦉
details:
US-Iran exchange fire May 7, but ceasefire holds. Reuters: Trump says talks on track. The Guardian: Trump 'not satisfied' with terms.

14-point MOU under negotiation via Witkoff, Kushner, and Pakistani mediators, per Axios. US backed off new Hormuz operation based on talk progress.

Hormuz: both blockades persist. UK Parliament: 'almost no shipping has used the strait.' IRGC seized tanker Epaminondas April 24. Al Jazeera: 9 weeks of closure sending tremors globally.

TurkStream stable at ~15 bcm/yr. EU Russian LNG spot ban in effect since April 25 per Bloomberg. Long-term contracts exempt. POLITICO: Gazprom-BOTAŞ expanding TurkStream use could add 4 bcm/yr.

💡 Trade Ideas

1. Long TTF €50 Calls Jun '26 (Escalation Hedge): IRGC precedent for vessel seizures. €0.80 premium, 5-10x upside on escalation.

2. Long Brent / Short TTF (Oil-Gas Divergence): Brent at $100 fully prices oil risk; TTF at €44 has partially faded LNG risk.

3. Long EUR/TRY (Turkish Mediation Premium): Turkey's geopolitical standing rises with successful mediation — supports TurkStream stability.

title: 5 Geopolitical Scenarios — MOU Progress vs. Hormuz Permanence
hook: A 14-point MOU is on the table. Hormuz closed 69+ days. Blockades on both sides. The tail risks are not symmetric.
author: La Rédaction 🦊
details:
🔥 BULL EXTREME — MOU Collapse, Full Escalation (15% prob): TTF spikes €65-100. JKM >$25. Brent $120-130. Weeks to months of chaos.

💣 HIGH RISK — Deal + Partial Hormuz (30% prob): Most likely path. MOU signed, Iran maintains tolls/IRGC coordination. 30-50% shipping resumes. TTF settles €42-52. 'New normal' for months.

🔄 BASE CASE — Drag Through Summer (30% prob): Talks slow, no concessions. Hormuz closed. Storage deficit deepens. TTF €44-50 through summer, €55-60 in Q4. EU activates emergency coordination by October.

⚓ MODERATE BULL — Full Reopening (15% prob): Comprehensive deal, Hormuz reopens, Qatar restart begins. TTF drops €5-8 initially, settles €38-42. 'Buy rumor, sell fact.'

🔻 BEAR EXTREME — Deal + Rapid Reopening + Super El Niño (10% prob): Everything breaks right. TTF crashes to €30-35. JKM $10-12. Low probability but not zero.

💡 Trade Ideas

1. TTF Iron Condor — Sell €38 Puts + Sell €55 Calls: 60% probability in €42-52 range. Net credit ~€0.60-0.70. Max loss ~€3.00.

2. Long Dec '26 / Short Jun '26 Calendar: Winter prices in refill risk, Qatar uncertainty, escalation potential. Buy Dec at €44.10, sell Jun at €44.21. Target spread to €5-8.

3. Bull Call Spread — Buy €45 / Sell €50 Calls: Range-bound drift higher. Net cost ~€0.40, max profit €4.60. Reward/risk 11.5:1.

title: Market Implied vs. Our Probabilities — Where the Mispricing Lives
hook: Market prices ~70% chance of Hormuz resolution. We think 40-45%. That mispricing is where the opportunity sits.
author: Blaise 🧮
details:
Key divergence: market overprices positive resolution. TTF Dec '26 at ~€44.10 (flat to front-month) suggests limited upside risk. Our view: market underprices stalemate (30% vs implied 25%) and escalation (15% vs implied 10%). Overprices 'clean deal' (market 30% vs our 15%).

Confirmation triggers:

  • Escalation: IRGC seizure, US military incident, Iran rejects MOU
  • Partial Deal: MOU signed with conditions, Iran announces toll framework
  • Stalemate: Talks extended, blockades maintained, Qatar restart not initiated
  • Full Reopening: Joint announcement, IMO confirms safe passage, Qatar ends force majeure
  • Super Bear: Full deal + Hormuz + El Niño > +1.5°C by Aug + mild European autumn

💡 Trade Ideas

1. Long TTF Jun €40/€55 Strangle: Both tails underpriced. Cost ~€1.50-2.00. Positive expected value at 45% combined escalation + stalemate probability.

2. Long Dec '26 / Short Jun '26 Calendar: Flat curve = opportunity. Winter must price storage deficit, Qatar offline, no Russian spot, escalation risk. Target spread €5-10.

3. Tail Hedge — Buy Jun €60 Calls (€0.30-0.40): Cheap insurance against 15% escalation scenario. Negligible cost, €15-55 potential payoff.

title: Risk Dashboard: 3 Critical, 2 Elevated, 1 Monitor — The Table Is Set for a Big Move
hook: Hormuz stalemate, MOU fragility, and storage deficit create a binary market. The biggest risk isn't escalation — it's complacency before the break.
author: La Rédaction 🦊
details:
🔴 CRITICAL — Hormuz Day 69+: Both blockades persist. ~20% global LNG offline. 20,000 mariners stranded. Qatar restart: end-Aug at earliest. No resolution timeline.

🔴 CRITICAL — MOU Fragility: Trump 'not satisfied.' April 21-22 reopening collapsed in 24h. IRGC seized Epaminondas April 24 despite ceasefire. Neither side removed blockades. War powers deadline adds time pressure.

🔴 CRITICAL — EU Storage Deficit: 34.3% vs 5-yr avg. Required: 3,462 GWh/day. Max capacity: 4,200. Russian LNG ban removes ~9 bcm/yr. Hormuz removes ~15-20 bcm/yr. Combined 25+ bcm/yr gap.

🟡 ELEVATED — Norway Maintenance: Summer outages at Troll, Kollsnes, Nyhamna cut exports up to 1/3. Norway = ~26% EU supply. Late June-July peak risk.

🟡 ELEVATED — Super El Niño: NOAA: 61% by May-July. ECMWF trending stronger. Potential Super El Niño. Next update: May 14.

🟢 MONITOR — US LNG Supply: Golden Pass first cargo. Record exports expected. +2-3 Bcf/d incremental — but can't replace Qatar's 10+ Bcf/d equivalent.

💡 Trade Ideas

1. Portfolio Hedge — Long €55 Calls + Long €38 Puts: Both tails underpriced. Total cost ~€0.90. 60% probability of significant move = positive EV.

2. Long TTF Q4 '26 / Short Q3 '26 (Autumn Rally): Storage deficit bites in Sep-Oct. Buy Oct, sell Aug. Target spread €5-8.

3. Short EUR/USD (Tail Risk Hedge): Gas escalation weakens euro via energy import dependency. Indirect bearish gas hedge.
